title: Missouri Personal Property Tax Calculator (Vehicle)
description: Estimate your Missouri vehicle personal property tax. Enter your car's market value and your county's total levy per $100. The tool applies the statewide 33⅓% assessment ratio to show your assessed value and annual tax.
answerSnippet: Missouri assesses vehicles at 33⅓% of market value. Tax = assessed value ÷ 100 × your county's levy. A $15,000 car is assessed at $5,000; at a $7.00 levy per $100 the annual tax is about $350.
intro:
Missouri charges an annual **personal property tax** on vehicles, collected by your **county collector**. The calculation has two steps set by different authorities.

First, the **assessed value** is fixed statewide by law: personal property like cars is assessed at **33⅓% of market value** (RSMo 137.115). A vehicle worth **$15,000** has an assessed value of **$5,000**. The market value used is generally the **N.A.D.A.** value as of **January 1**.

Second, your **total levy** — the combined tax rate for your **county, city, school district**, and other local entities — is applied per **$100** of that assessed value. Levies **vary widely** by address, so this tool asks you to enter your local levy (replace the placeholder with your county's actual rate).

Enter your vehicle's **market value** and your **county's total levy** to see your assessed value and estimated annual tax.
keyTakeaway: Missouri vehicle tax = **(market value × 33⅓%) ÷ 100 × your county's total levy**. The **33⅓%** assessment ratio is set statewide by law; the **levy** is set locally and varies by county, city, and school district. Assessment date is **January 1**, and declarations are typically due by **April 1** — get your exact levy from your county collector.

explanation:
## How Missouri vehicle tax is calculated

```
Assessed value = market value × 33⅓%   (RSMo 137.115, personal property)
Annual tax     = assessed value ÷ 100 × total levy ($ per $100)
```

The **33⅓% ratio is statewide** and does not change by county. What changes is the **levy** — the sum of all the taxing districts at your address (county, city, school, library, fire, etc.). That is why two people with identical cars can owe very different amounts.

## Assessed value at 33⅓%

| Market value | Assessed value (33⅓%) |
|---|---|
| $6,000 | $2,000 |
| $12,000 | $4,000 |
| $15,000 | $5,000 |
| $24,000 | $8,000 |
| $30,000 | $10,000 |

## Where the tax varies

Only the **levy** varies. A $5,000 assessed value at a **$6.00** levy is **$300**; at **$8.50** it is **$425**. Metro counties (St. Louis, St. Charles, Jackson, Greene) publish their combined rates per $100 — get yours from the **county collector** for an exact figure.

## Key dates

- **Assessment date:** January 1 (you are taxed on what you owned that day).
- **Declaration deadline:** typically **March 1–April 1** — file your personal property declaration with the assessor.
- **Payment:** bills go out in the fall and are generally **due December 31**; late payment adds penalties.

## A note on value

Missouri assessors generally use the **N.A.D.A.** trade-in value as of January 1. Recent law has aimed to smooth year-to-year swings in vehicle values, but the **33⅓%** ratio itself is unchanged.

## Disclaimer

Educational estimate. The default levy is an example only — your actual tax depends on your county's official combined levy, the assessor's value for your specific vehicle, and any waivers or proration. Confirm with your county collector and assessor.

faq.q: How is Missouri vehicle property tax calculated?
faq.a: Your vehicle is assessed at **33⅓% of market value**, then taxed at your county's **total levy per $100** of that assessed value. A $15,000 car is assessed at $5,000; at a $7.00 levy the tax is **$350**.

faq.q: What is the assessment ratio for cars in Missouri?
faq.a: **33⅓%** (one-third) of market value, set statewide by **RSMo 137.115**. It is the same in every county — only the levy rate changes by location.

faq.q: Why is my neighbor's car tax different?
faq.a: Because the **levy varies by taxing district**. Even within a county, your city, school district, and special districts change the combined rate, so identical cars can owe different amounts.

faq.q: What market value does Missouri use?
faq.a: Assessors generally use the **N.A.D.A.** trade-in value as of **January 1**. You are taxed based on what you owned on that date, regardless of whether you sell the car later in the year.

faq.q: When is Missouri personal property tax due?
faq.a: Bills are mailed in the fall and are generally **due by December 31**. You must also file a **personal property declaration** with your assessor, typically by **March 1–April 1**.

faq.q: Where do I find my county's levy rate?
faq.a: Your **county collector or assessor** publishes the combined levy per $100 for each taxing district. Many counties also offer an online estimator. Enter that rate into this calculator for an accurate figure.

faq.q: Do I owe tax if I moved to Missouri recently?
faq.a: You are taxed where you **lived and garaged the vehicle on January 1**. If you moved into Missouri after January 1, you generally would not owe Missouri personal property tax until the following year — confirm with the assessor.

faq.q: How can I lower or waive the tax?
faq.a: If you did not own any taxable personal property on January 1 (for example, a new resident), you may qualify for a **tax waiver** from the assessor. Otherwise the tax is based on the fixed 33⅓% ratio and your local levy.
